message.content: The lion (Panthera leo) and the zebra (Equus quagga) diverged from a common ancestor that is shared by all placental mammals. In other words, the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived roughly 100–120 million years ago (in the early Cretaceous). This ancestor is not a named species but a hypothetical ancestral mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to modern carnivores (like lions) and odd‑toed ungulates (like zebras).
